new_title: Jobe Bellingham joining Jude in England squad is 'beautiful', says Tuchel - as it happened
old_text:
Jobe Bellingham and Josh King called up by England
Jobe Bellingham and Josh King are the headline names after Thomas Tuchel handed both uncapped midfielders call-ups to his England squad for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. Borussia Dortmund's Bellingham, 21, joins his brother Jude in the senior set-up after impressing as captain of the Under-21s.
King's rise has been just as rapid. The 19-year-old has become a fixture in Fulham's midfield this season, and his two Premier League goals make him their top league scorer. He travelled with England's preparation squad before the summer's World Cup and has kept catching the eye for the Under-21s.
Michael Carrick is asked for some thoughts about the aforementioned Ferguson on the 40th anniversary of his appointment at Old Trafford:
"What's not been said already?" Carrick begins. "It's something worth celebrating as a club, 40 years this weeks since he came here, the impact ... all that's he's left for others to carry forward is incredible. I am probably closer to him now, and speak more to him now, that I did when I was playing.
"The impact he had on me as an individual was massive ...
"Those habits you picked up over time from him and tried to emulate ... then you move on more into a friendship, which is really nice."
"It's up to us to take it forward. As a one off night it was fantastic ... to finish so strongly ... I thought we played really really well and deserved the game ... it was nice for the supporters to have that feeling ... but nothing's achieved yet, it's one moment, we need to use it to move forward. We need more of it, for sure."
The lovely people at the Guardian Research Department have flagged that it is the 40-year anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson's appointment as Manchester United manager. The news to appoint the then up-and-coming Scot from Aberdeen was worthy of the front page on 6 November 1986. Here's the cutting:
Portugal pledged to honour Cristiano Ronaldo as manager Jorge Jesus named his first squad since the 41-year-old announced his international retirement.
Jesus faced a barrage of questions about the rift that preceded the departure of Ronaldo after the forward announced his retirement decision on social media on Thursday, ending a Portugal career spanning 234 appearances and 146 goals.
Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca promised to celebrate Ronaldo's contribution, although there was no word on whether the forward would agree to a farewell appearance. "No tribute will ever be enough to thank him for everything he has done for Portuguese football, for Portugal," Proenca said before the squad announcement.
"We will do everything we can to honour the legacy he leaves us. Everything he has done deserves to be honoured and celebrated."
Jesus selected seven new faces, including five players from the Under-21s, for November's Nations League matches against Wales and Denmark. Reuters
Arsenal midfielder Max Dowman has been called up to England's Under-21 squad for the first time.
The 16-year-old, previously capped at Under-17 and Under-19 level, is already on the radar of senior boss Thomas Tuchel owing to his achievements at Arsenal. Dowman has now been named in Lee Carsley's group for games against Portugal and France this month.
With captain Jobe Bellingham promoted to the senior set-up, midfielders Trey Nyoni, Harrison Armstrong and Divine Mukasa remain in the group following their step up from the Under-20s. Brighton's Jack Hinshelwood is named in the squad after missing the last camp due to injury
Tottenham striker Mikey Moore, who is on loan at FC Koln, also receives his first call-up. Will Lankshear, the striker who has scored 15 goals in 16 games since joining Middlesbrough from Spurs in the summer, has not been included after missing Boro's midweek clash with Wrexham through injury.
Carsley's men play friendlies against Portugal on Friday 13 November and France three days later, both at Ashton Gate as they prepare for next summer's Under-21s European Championship.
Luis de la Fuente has called up three uncapped players for his Spain squad to take on England and Czechia in the Nations League.
Jacobo Ramon, who played in Como's record-equalling 9-1 Champions League win over Lens, plus Real Betis pair Alvaro Valles and Marc Roca are in line for debuts after being named in a squad missing the injured trio of Rodri, Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo. AFP
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner has warned his players they are not at a "spa and wellness hotel" and has demanded they improve on a difficult start to the campaign.
Forest welcome Manchester City to the City Ground on Saturday, with the visitors looking to bounce back themselves, following successive Premier League defeats.
Glasner says he is still trying to create a culture at his new club:
We are not a spa and wellness hotel where you like to relax and enjoy. But of course, as I mentioned, we are also not the military. We need to find in-between. What I want is to get every player having this intrinsic motivation, to want to improve his game.
'Come on, coach, tell me what do I have to do to get better?' And this is what I hope, and I'm pretty sure we will create. That we will be more challenged by the players in the future.
Dedic set to escape Newcastle sanction over carrying bow and arrow
Newcastle's Amar Dedic is unlikely to face a club sanction after being spotted holding a bow and arrow in the Northumberland countryside and sparking a major police pursuit involving an armed response unit.
Dedic is expected to start Newcastle's match at Fulham on Saturday following an incident that at one point saw six patrol cars pursue the Bosnia right-back back to his home on the upmarket Darras Hall estate, just outside Ponteland.
A bit more Maresca on Nico O'Reilly, who has been left out of the latest England squad. The Manchester City manager is not concerned about his form and believes the 21-year-old could benefit from a rest during the international break:
It's what he needs. With Nico, it's quite easy. Since we started the season, between his back (injury) before the Coventry game and some more problems unfortunately, he's not 100%.
In the last game I really liked him, I thought he was playing a very good game and this is what we need from Nico.
Let's just keep him fit because we know how good he is and no doubt in the future that he will be back with the international team. Now use that break to do the right things in terms of therapy and these kind of things and be 100% after the international break.
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is confident goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma will get back to his best with little guidance in his native Italian.
Donnarumma's form has been under scrutiny after a number of mistakes in recent games. Maresca has continued to back his first choice throughout his troubles and has no plans for in-depth conversations with his fellow Italian. He said:
It's much easier for me with the language! We are (having conversations) but there are players who when they make mistakes, you need conversations with them and there are players that when they make a mistake you just need eye contact to understand that he recognises and he knows.
With Gigio it's quite easy because every time he has made some mistake or something that was not correct, he recognises immediately. I spoke with Gigio but sometimes you don't need to be so deep with some players because they know they have made a mistake and recognise that. Just try to avoid that and move on.
Overall he's good. He's quite relaxed in terms of he recognises that he has done some mistakes but at the same time he has also made some good saves. It's just a matter of balance - try to avoid mistakes and continue to do the right things.
It appears Coady has his ducks in a row, a new podcast from Gareth Southgate's production company, 1071 Media, was announced yesterday, in partnership with Sky Sports, where the recently retired defender will appear alongside familiar face Mark Chapman. The Football Dugout will feature in-depth, tactical conversations with managers, players, coaches, and sporting directors, according the blurb. It's the one we've all been asking for.
For me, Coady will always be fondly remembered for hitting an astonishing 23 mentions of 'the football club/a/the/this club' in five minutes and 28 seconds of his signing announcement at Wrexham. Inspirational football clubbing:
The former Wolves man has called it a day at 33 having featured for Charlton in the second half of the last Championship season. He earned the last of his 10 England caps in 2022.
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is on track for a "full recovery" after a lengthy absence following his collapse at a training session, his assistant Aaron Danks has confirmed.
Kompany has been out of action for two weeks since collapsing at a reserve team training session on 23 October. He was hospitalised and treated for meningeal irritation, which is an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord.
"I've had a few really good phone calls with Vince," Danks said. "He seems very positive and appears to be well on the way to a full recovery. The international break provides a good opportunity to reflect and see when he can return."
It's becoming pretty clear that Tuchel values commitment and availability, he's given a long answer on that subject when asked about the standby list. Here are the key quotes:
It is always about the ones who are in camp, who don't withdraw and walk the talk, come to camp and show that it matters.
I think that [message] is naturally coming through. That was always the message very, very early that is matters if you are in camp.
The last camp was an excellent one and the trust and belief is in the players who were there.
Kobbie Mainoo has had a "difficult spell" with his club and missed games, says Tuchel explaining the decision to pick others ahead of the Manchester United midfielder. Tuchel says it is time for Ben White "to write a new chapter" with England and helps them in a position where they have a "bizarre" amount of injuries.
A bit more on Palmer, Tuchel re-emphasised that the Chelsea player "misses too many opportunities to impress", while later clarifying that the door was always open, the England manager said:
I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp, it was two and a half weeks and the players and the boys who were in campo built something extraordinary.
That's why the credit goes to them, the trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.
So it's not personal and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.
On the question of who will replace Bukayo Saka with Noni Madueke not selected, Tuchel says Morgan Rogers is now the first choice with Rio Ngumoha as backup and Josh King as another option.
First of all Lee [Carsley] is speaking very highly of him for the Under-21s for a while now. He is the standout player. He is the captain of the Under-21s so I think the door should always be open and the pathway should always be open for special performances over a long period of time and that is what Jobe has done.
He found his way and his rhythm with Dortmund, where he has had an excellent start to the season. He's a regular starter there and very influential and there's an opportunity.
There is an opportunity coming through the pathway, coming on his own merit, Jobe deserves to make an impressive for us. We're happy to have him in camp and see what he can do for us.
On the first question of Palmer's absence, Tuchel said:
It's enough No 10s and we stick to the guys we had in camp. Camp was excellent and we were happy with the last two and half weeks we had togther. The impact of the players was immense throughout the whole camp and that's why we stick mainly with the group.
We have Josh King in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He's kind of an extra player that we use, we have training numbers and he can cover all eventualities because Josh can play all four positions, so that's basically the reason.
Good morning, I've just seen Jude Bellingham has posted a sweet picture of him and Jobe as boys with matching Birmingham shirts and dyed blue hair. In the often cynical world of football, that is quite a sweet family moment. Who were the last brothers to play for England, was it the Nevilles?
Some reaction from Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa following Josh King's call-up by England.
"Yes, I think it's a special moment for him, for us as a club and obviously for our supporters.
"I think Josh is the pride of our club and our supporters. He came to this club when he was eight-years-old. Now, when you look at him, how he's playing, how he's performing, we are really proud of him.
"I think it's a big step for him and I'm so happy for him because he's a very humble kid. You can see every day he wants to improve, he wants to work, he wants to become a better player every day. So I think it's a special day for him and for all of us."
What do we make of that then? Josh King a better player than Cole Palmer? Looks like this goes beyond just playing ability. Tuchel's press conference is set for 11am so we'll see how he explains what looks like a huge snub.
The other big news in Tuchel's squad announcement is that there is again no place for Cole Palmer. Other surprise omissions include Noni Madueke and Kobbie Mainoo.

Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Marc Guéhi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Jarell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)
Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), James Garner (Everton), Josh King (Fulham), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Borussia Dortmund's Bellingham, 21, joins his brother Jude in the senior set-up after impressing as captain of the Under-21s.

Fifa wants talks with the IOC over restricting the Olympic women's football tournament to under-23s owing to concerns over fixture congestion and the workload of senior players. Here's Matt Hughes' exclusive.
The death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda is still hard to comprehend. Utterly tragic.
Sid Lowe: "Football is supposed to be a safe space, a refuge, an escape. All those lines about giving your life to the game are not supposed to be literal. This didn't make sense. The images and the outcome shocked; the contradictory combination of the improbability and the plausibility of it all made it harder still to come to terms with: this couldn't happen yet it could have happened to anyone."
Frank Lampard's return to Everton kicks off this week's 10 things column. Also... Glasner sparking Forest fire, Zubimendi and Kroupi in spotlight and Carrick v Emery.
The Premier League weekend action starts tonight with Everton v Coventry. A couple of things...
1) Get those fantasy teams sorted in time.
2) This City Is Ours will have to wait until full-time. Tonight's Merseyside turf war comes first - follow it via our MBM.
If Frank Lampard's visitors get the win they'll move to 12 points. Andrew Beasley reveals why that's significant.
A round-up of last night's action in Europe. That's now seven wins on the trot for Bournemouth in all competitions but they're not happy up in Sunderland.
Paul MacInnes was at Selhurst Park to see 10-man Palace snatch a draw.
"After being outplayed by a side currently in the bottom half of the Bundesliga, and a goal down from the seventh minute, Palace looked to have lost all hope in this fixture when Adam Wharton was dismissed with 13 minutes to go..."
Some talking points ahead of the England squad announcement which we're expecting at 10am GMT. England go into the final two games on nine points after three wins and a loss.
Cole Palmer. The Chelsea manpulled out of the September/October squad through injury, which drew a frustrated response from Thomas Tuchel, who said the 24-year-old misses too many camps. Does he get another chance?
Saka out, so who comes in on the right? Bukayo Saka misses this international break after picking up a quadriceps problem in the 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich. Arsenal colleague Noni Madueke looks the obvious replacement.
The goalkeeper debate. Jordan Pickford faces genuine competition for the No 1 spot for the first time in his England career, with James Trafford having started two of the four autumn games. Dean Henderson is also likely to return after recovering from injury.
Will Lankshear. Could the youngstriker, who left Tottenham for Middlesbrough in the summer, get a surprise call-up. Taken under the wing of Harry Kane and all that. Lankshear's tally of 15 goals in 16 matches for Boro this season is certainly Kane-like.
If England's Champions League sides delivered a mixed bag earlier in the week, Thursday's Europa League action was no different.
Bournemouth's winning streak continued, 10-man Crystal Palace scraped a last-gasp draw while there were boos at Sunderland after a home loss to Dinamo Zagreb. Elsewhere, there was a rousing comeback win for Celtic and Brighton still don't know what it's like to concede a goal in the Conference League after a 1-0 win at Getafe.
But that's last night's news. Football doesn't hang around and today the focus is on the announcement of England's squad for the final two Nations League group games against Croatia and Spain. Expect the white smoke around 10am.
That latest pesky international break starts next week but before then it's another round of hot Premier League action. We'll have build-up and managers talking throughout the day.

Uncapped Paris FC forward Pablo Pagis was surprisingly summoned by France coach Zinedine Zidane for his latest squad.
Pagis, 23, made the 23-man list after Paris Saint-Germain's Maghnes Akliouche was ruled out by a calf injury. Zidane said Pagis has an "interesting" and "different profile" that he wants to assess.
Pagis joined Paris FC in the summer after Lorient stay in Ligue 1 following promotion the previous season. Last season Pagis, who can play across the front line, scored 10 goals in Ligue 1 and has two this campaign. Paris FC are currently fourth in the league, with former Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior making positive return to French football.
France tops their Nations league group with 10 points from four games and travel to Italy on 12 November before hosting Turkey three days later.
Zidane is dealing with a flurry of injuries as William Saliba, Jules Koundé, Maxence Lacroix, Manu Koné, Ousmane Dembélé and Esteban Lepaul have been ruled out. AP
Another club playing in Europe and struggling are Sunderland. Regis Le Bris admitted his side cannot "let negativity creep in" as the Black Cats navigate a tough run of form.
Sunderland's unbeaten run in the Europa League was ended on Thursday night as they endured their first defeat in the competition with a 2-0 loss to Dinamo Zagreb to add to their concerns, with the team booed by fans at the Stadium of Light.
They languish at the bottom of the Premier League table and a meeting against fourth-placed Chelsea is their next test on Sunday before the international break, but Le Bris insisted his players are "ready for the next fight".
"It's part of the journey. Often when we get successes we think about the last part of the journey but we forget how tough it was before, so it's a good example," Le Bris said. "Obviously it's not a comfortable period, we don't like it, but at the same time we have to show the way and keep the energy high.
"When I wake up in the morning I have this energy and I have to give it to the players, and I think this morning it was a bit painful once again but they are ready for the next fight.
"We have to keep the clarity about what we have to improve as a team because it's fair to say at the minute we are a bit too exposed, we concede too many goals and it's always a race after the score.
"It's important also to back each other and we can't let the negativity creep in, it's not possible, otherwise you kill the togetherness, the creativity, the energy. So it's part of the journey and it's a strong reminder about our pillars, how do we want to achieve our goals."
Pierre Sage insists he remains more concerned about Crystal Palace than his own increasingly uncertain future in south London. The French boss' side are in the relegation zone heading into Sunday's Selhurst Park clash with Liverpool, with just two wins from their opening nine matches.
Unlike Thursday's 1-1 Europa League draw with Hoffenheim - which required a last-gasp Daichi Kamada equaliser - Sage will not have Jean-Philippe Mateta at his disposal, with the French striker serving the first game of his three-match ban for his red card at Tottenham.
"Same reply, I'm worried about the team, about what happens daily with the team, with the players" Sage said. "My situation is less important than the situation of the club, and I am really honest with that.
"Football is not a hard job. I don't save lives, I don't work in a mine. I have to find good solutions, that's all."
It is unclear whether loanee defender Axel Disasi will be recalled. Disasi played in last weekend's defeat at Tottenham but was not in the squad for the Europa League fixture against Hoffenheim, with reports suggesting he was dropped for turning up late to a team meating. Sage's batted away questions on Disasi, saying: "It's an internal decision. I don't want to comment."
Gary O'Neil does not have a bad word to say about former club Bournemouth despite the Cherries binning him off after he kept them in the top flight. O'Neil's Tractor Boys face Bournemouth on Sunday's clash at Portman Road.
After a slow start, Marco Rose will take Bournemouth to Ipswich on a seven-match winning streak and newly promoted Ipswich are braced for a difficult test.
"Bournemouth are obviously in a very good place at the moment," O'Neil told a press conference. "I've watched them and saw their game against Sparta Prague on Thursday. It was only a competitive game for a while. The squad they have put together over the years is very impressive.
"They made plenty of changes for the Europa League game and still looked strong. The new coach has had an impact. Clean sheets not easy to come by, especially in the Premier League and they've picked up a good few, but our focus is always on us.
"We will get to Portman Road and do everything we can to put in a strong performance and get three points."
If Everton v Coventry - the Frank Lampard derby that isn't Chelsea v West Ham - doesn't take your fancy this evening and a lower-league clash in the Championship isn't getting you hot under the collar, then there are two FA Cup first round fixtures this evening. John Brewin's excellent cup picks in today's Football Daily do not feature either of Bristol Rovers v Cambridge or Oxford City v Leicester, but the latter is decent chance for a giant killing. Oxford City are 17th in National League North and few need reminding of how recently Leicester were winning this competition. League One Leicester are facing a plastic pitch and crowd at very close quarters at the The MGroup Stadium, which will be packed. This absolutely screams nervy first 20 minutes for Leicester and it'll be up to the semi-pros to take advantage. I'll be watching.
Rice determined to hit 'another level', says Arteta
Mikel Arteta has lauded Declan Rice's "desperate" determination to improve after the midfielder was one of five Arsenal players called up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad.
Rice has contributed five Premier League assists this season - the most of any player - and a Champions League goal. Asked what had changed in Rice's performance, Arteta said: "The mentality to go out and win football matches and to add another level to his game, another kind of threat and be much more unpredictable, and we've been working a lot on that.
"He's desperate to improve every part of his game, and we need to do that while we maintain so many incredible things that he's already done, but he's on the right trajectory."
Arteta agreed Rice had strengthened his ball progression, and explained his thinking behind dropping the 27-year-old deeper. "We cannot restrict his qualities and his capacities," Arteta said. "He can drop back, he can progress play. He can drop back, he can carry the ball, he can be incredible in transition.
"He can win duels. He can produce passes by arriving, by playing far, by crossing the ball left or right, it doesn't matter. On set pieces [too], he's got a lot to offer. His shooting ability from long range as well is something that we need to use more." Press Association
Spanish opposition leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo says he would be willing to withdraw Spain as a host of the 2030 World Cup should Fifa award the final to Morocco.
Fifa are yet to declare a venue for the final of the 2030 World Cup, hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain. Feijoo, who leads the conservative Popular Party, said that it was "inarguable" that Spain should host the event.
"Spain must host the World Cup final. And if it doesn't, in my opinion, Spain shouldn't take part in organising the World Cup," said Feijoo in an interview with El Chiringuito.
When asked if he would look to withdraw Spain as a host if he were in power, Feijoo responded, "Yes, the answer is yes."
Feijoo is the main opposition to socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who said in a September interview with Cadena SER that he was "working for it [the final] to be held in Spain". National team manager Luis de la Fuente told a press conference on Friday that he had made his opinion clear that "the final should be played in Spain".
Wrexham have announced the departure of CEO Michael Williamson. Director Shaun Harvey, once of Bradford, Leeds and the EFL will take over as acting CEO.
Co-Chairs Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds have issued a joint statement: "We thank Michael Williamson for his two years at Wrexham and for his work taking the club from League 1 to the Championship.
"Since our takeover five years ago, Wrexham have had historic success on the pitch and won hearts all over the globe. We remain focused on our most important task: to make the Wrexham community proud. Shaun Harvey has been an integral part of this journey from the beginning, and we know Shaun will give every support to Phil Parkinson and the lads on the pitch while keeping the broader Wrexham community roaring us on."
Before moving to Wrexham, Williamson held senior positions at Inter Milan and in Major League Soccer. He was named Football Industry Leader of the Year in 2025
Tuchel: Bellingham brothers in England squad is 'beautiful'
Thomas Tuchel has told the BBC that the Bellingham brothers' is "a beautiful story".
"They are both good for each other. My understanding is they are very close. It makes life easier for Jobe to come into camp and know his brother is one of the key players in our team. So, that will hopefully help him, but don't forget he is here on his own merits, and he is not here because of his brother."
Tuchel selected the Dortmund midfielder, who plays deeper than his big brother.
Jobe is the current captain of the England Under-21 side and Tuchel is a confirmed fan. "He's the standout player. He's the captain, so the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time. That's what Jobe has done on top of it. He found his way, he found his rhythm with Dortmund. He's had an excellent start to his season, is a regular starter and influential."
Fifa news, their top legal man is leaving: "Emilio García Silvero has expressed his wish to embark on a new chapter in his career and return to Spain after 15 years of working abroad in the service of international football," read a statement.
As head of legal and compliance unit, García oversaw tournament disciplinary cases, transfer market rules and contractual disputes worldwide, and steered moving the soccer body's lawyers from Zurich to Miami in 2023.
"It has truly been a dream to work alongside colleagues from around the world to improving the regulatory framework of international football," García said in the Fifa statement.
García had previously worked with Gianni Infantino when both were at Uefa and followed him to Zurich in 2018. (AFP)
China is in contact with Real Madrid and La Liga over the fallout from Kylian Mbappé's remarks about Mao Zedong.
"There are no negotiations, but there is communication, based on mutual understanding," China's ambassador to Spain Yao Jing said. "This unfortunate incident hurt the feelings of many people in China, who now have to come to terms with the current situation.
La Liga, Real Madrid and the French footballer all subsequently apologised. China's state broadcaster CCTV suspended its coverage of LaLiga and several Chinese brands dropped Mbappe from their marketing campaigns. Streaming platform Migu omitted Real Madrid's match against Racing Santander last weekend while showing other Spanish league games. (Reuters)
Jorge Jesus has been talking about the international retirement of Cristiano Ronaldo as Portugal prepare to face Denmark and Wales in the Nations League.
"Of course I thought he would come back, of course I thought I would call him up, of course I thought I would speak with him, but you have to respect him. He decided that it was the moment to leave the national team.
"Sooner or later it had to happen. He felt it was the best moment to leave, and we have to respect that, while never forgetting what he represented for Portugal. All my decisions were made with the team in mind. I do not feel guilty in any way about his departure."
Enzo Maresca had this to say on Phil Foden's continued absence from the England squad:
I don't know why [he was left out], but we are happy with Phil. My duty is to help him get back playing his best for Manchester City and hopefully he can then get back into the England team.
Brentford manager Keith Andrews has promised his team will take their "A game" to the battle of the B-teams with Brighton.
Brighton are third, Brentford are sixth. Andrews: "I think they're playing really, really well. The way they're organised in every facet of the game is very impressive.
"They've clearly got really good spirit, they've recruited well, they've got an honesty around the group and they're clearly playing with a lot of confidence. We'll need to bring our A game on Sunday to get the result that we want.
"You have to be very understanding of what they're capable of, what they're doing consistently, how they can tweak, what they tweak and when they tweak it. We're quite flexible and adaptable ourselves in terms of what we do and how we can do it. We've got the tools to cause them problems; we've got the tools to cause any team problems, but we'll need to play very well."
Jeff Rueter reports as the NWSL playoffs get underway.
Gotham FC play Seattle Reign on Sunday.
And so, the project evolved: Gotham won a global competition for Sam Kerr's services, bringing the club's record goalscorer back as a free agent after her time at Chelsea. How long could they keep four Best XI caliber attacking players getting their expected looks? That was a two-fronted task the club embraced.
At Tottenham, after a fine display against Crystal Palace last week, there's much excitement about Luca Williams-Barnett. Will Roberto De Zerbi start him?
"The pre-season, it was clear (he is) a special talent. You recognise the special talent immediately and he doesn't need to show something special, you understand? Everything that he does (is enough) and he is one of the special talents," De Zerbi said.
"The next step he has to enjoy, he has to follow the older players, the players with more experience like (Andy) Robertson, (James) Maddison, Ben Davies and to find the time to play. It is my responsibility because when you manage young players and so big talents like Luca, it is a bigger responsibility for me.
"He has to be ready when he goes on the pitch. I think it (does) not depend on the result, he can play from the beginning. Before the Chelsea game, I thought to play with him in the first XI, but in the end you have to find the right moment and for them also. I think the age is not so important. The most important is the quality, personality, the behaviour on the pitch and the qualities. And Luca has all of these qualities."
Bradley Barcola played as a striker for Liverpool against Fenerbahce, and it didn't go well. Andoni Iraola has been asked about that. "No, Bradley is a winger. Mostly he has played as a left winger and sometimes as a right winger, but also has played for PSG as a striker, which is something I wanted to try.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner has warned his players they are not at a "spa and wellness hotel" and has demanded they improve on a difficult start to the campaign. Forest welcome Manchester City to the City Ground on Saturday, with the visitors looking to bounce back themselves, following successive Premier League defeats. Glasner says he is still trying to create a culture at his new club: We are not a spa and wellness hotel where you like to relax and enjoy. But of course, as I mentioned, we are also not the military. We need to find in-between. What I want is to get every player having this intrinsic motivation, to want to improve his game. 'Come on, coach, tell me what do I have to do to get better?' And this is what I hope, and I'm pretty sure we will create. That we will be more challenged by the players in the future.
